title: Add snapshot tests for runner executor prompt builders
problem: runner/executor.py::build_step_prompt and runner/executor.py::build_verify_prompt build the literal text the model sees for every create/modify/delete step and every verify step. Currently they have ZERO test coverage. A typo, an accidentally-dropped section, or a regression in the instruction text would silently degrade every subsequent runner run with no test signal.
description:
Add a new TestPromptBuilders class to runner/test_executor.py covering both prompt builders.

Strategy: structural invariant assertions, NOT byte-exact snapshots. Byte-exact snapshots are too brittle and break on every wording tweak. Instead, assert the presence of expected section headers and verify that step / spec field values get interpolated correctly.

For build_step_prompt, write tests for each of the four non-test/verify actions (create, modify, delete) that assert:
- the rendered prompt contains '## Step: <description>'
- it contains '**Type:**', '**Action:**', '**Files:**'
- the files list is comma-joined
- it contains '## Code specification' followed by the literal   step['code_spec'] text
- it contains '## Instructions'
- it contains the action-specific instruction sentence   ('Create the file(s)', 'Read the existing file(s)',   'Delete the file(s)')
- it ends with the 'Write the actual code' tail

For build_verify_prompt, mirror the same shape: read the current implementation in runner/executor.py and assert each section header + each substituted field appears.

Use a small fixture step + fixture spec defined as helper functions in the test class. Don't refactor production code.
context: Filed as scribe TODO #251. Test-only PR — zero behavior change. Closes the largest test-coverage gap in the runner with the smallest possible blast radius.
